court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: M.J. Omkumar vs The District Revenue Officer (Stamp)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: M.J. Omkumar and M.J. Govindakumar (sons of M. Jayaraman)
parties.respondent_defendant: The District Revenue Officer (Stamp) and The Sub Registrar, Tiruttani

facts_of_case: Petitioners are sons of M. Jayaraman who executed a Settlement Deed in their favour. Notice was issued by the Second Respondent claiming deficit stamp duty and registration charges. Petitioners claim to have made representation but did not receive response.

legal_principles.principle: Children born out of a void marriage are legitimate.
legal_principles.held: Section 16 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 makes the legal position abundantly clear that the children born out of 'void' marriage are 'legitimate'.
cited_cases: Rameshwari Devi -vs- State of Bihar, (2000) 2 SCC 431
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining the legal status of children

legal_principles.principle: The legitimacy of children is not affected by the marital status of their parents.
legal_principles.held: Notwithstanding that a marriage is null and void, any child of such marriage who would have been legitimate if the marriage had been valid, shall be legitimate.
cited_cases: Rameshwari Devi -vs- State of Bihar, (2000) 2 SCC 431
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining the legal status of children

outcome.final_order: The writ petition is allowed, calling for the entire records connected with the impugned order passed by the Second Respondent and quashing the same.

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition for judicial review
advising on stamp duty and registration procedures
